definition: A subject is "an entity that changes over time": each employee is a member whose attribute changes open new validity intervals, which Visier's glossary maps to a slowly changing dimension type 2.
grain: One row per employment record per job version
notes: This inventory is a rehearsal: Nodewell Labs is fictional, its data synthetic and its Visier tenant hypothetical, so the Visier side of every row is Visier's documented definition, not an export from a real tenant. Same shape. Visier keeps each record "valid until it's not"; dim_employee closes each version with an inclusive valid_to (9999-12-31 while open), taken from the HRIS effective dates (valid time). A member is an employee_id (Visier's EmployeeID); a rehire gets a new employee_id and person_id links the two, so the warehouse can count records or people. Visier also keeps record time (when it received the data), which the warehouse only approximates with load timestamps. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Platform/key-terms.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/data/data-loads.htm

visier_item: Employment Start (Employee Start in some docs)
definition: The hire event and the Employee subject's conception event, which opens a member's validity; "Hire Date, Hire Type, and Time to Hire are properties of the Employee Start event".
grain: One row per FTE employment record starting, from 2023-10-01
notes: Visier docs use both names for this event: take the one the tenant's Data Model API listing returns. fct_hires is FTE-only and starts on 2023-10-01, when the warehouse history begins; earlier starts exist only as dim_employee.hire_date. A rehire is a start (new employee_id). Q3 2026: 45 FTE starts. Visier's benchmark list has an Employee Starts Rate; it is not built here. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/analytic-objects/analytic-object-settings.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/getting%20started/objects-visier-cloud.htm https://www.visier.com/docs/definitions/successfactors https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Visier%20People%20Metrics/benchmarks/benchmarks%20visier.htm

definition: "An event that records the termination of an employee": the ending event of the Employee subject, with attributes such as Employee Exit Reason and Employee Exit Type.
grain: One row per FTE exit event
notes: termination_date is the last day employed and the person leaves headcount the next day. For metrics that track movement Visier counts an exit on April 30 in May; the warehouse counts an exit in the period of termination_date, except the month-to-month walk test (assert_headcount_reconciles_month_to_month), which already buckets it on termination_date + 1. Visier's system-events page says the same for turnover: "Terminations on the last day of the month may count toward the next month's turnover", and the system "treats the last working day as the termination date" (it may move a first-non-working-day date back one day). The "may", and the page listing these among scenarios that trigger system termination events, leave the tenant's setup an open question for the client. No FTE exit fell on 2026-06-30 or on a Q3 2026 month end, so the rule moves nothing in fct_terminations for Q3 2026; under Visier's default population the 10 interns who left on 2026-08-31 would move from August to September (still inside Q3; see reconciliation.md). Contractor and intern exits are left out of fct_terminations; whether the tenant's exit metrics include them is an open question. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/analytic-objects/events-create.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/analytic-objects/system-events.htm

definition: Selection concept that defines the headcount population; in Visier's documented example, employees whose Employment Status is "Active" or "On Notice".
bigquery_target: analytics.fct_headcount_daily (a row for every day from hire_date to termination_date) with is_fte; analytics.dim_employee.is_current for the reporting date
grain: One row per employment record per day employed
notes: The source has only Active and Terminated statuses, so there is no On Notice or leave state to include or exclude: an employee is active from hire_date through termination_date inclusive. The warehouse adds employment_type = 'fte' on top (see Employment Type). Open question: the tenant's concept configuration (On Notice, leave, contingent workers) and whether its Headcount metric was edited. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/concepts/selection/selection-configure.htm https://docs.visier.com/swp/Organization%20Design/data-requirements.htm

definition: Tenant-specific property to confirm in the tenant's Data Model API listing: whether the employment record is a full-time employee, a contractor or an intern.
grain: One value per employment record (per requisition on the ATS side)
notes: The main population difference. Warehouse headcount, attrition and hiring metrics count employment_type = 'fte' only; Visier's Headcount "includes all current employees" by default, and customers can edit it, for example to exclude contingent workers. On 2026-09-30 that is 21 contractors (no interns that day). Decision: see Headcount. The full-time count stays, labelled 'Headcount (full-time employees)', beside a count that follows the tenant's Headcount population (its isActiveEmployee concept plus any filter added to the Headcount formula), recorded once both have been read. Source: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Platform/use-cases/build.htm

definition: "The number of employees in the organization": on Employee filterBy(isActiveEmployee) aggregate count(EmployeeID), taken at the last instant of the period; additive across dimensions, not over time.
bigquery_target: analytics.fct_headcount_daily (countif(is_fte) on the period's last snapshot_date); analytics.rpt_workforce_daily.headcount
grain: One value per day; use the last day of the period
notes: Both count people, one per active employment record: the source has no FTE factor, and 'FTE' in the warehouse means employment_type = 'fte', not a sum of FTE fractions. The difference is the population: 2026-09-30 = 595 FTEs against 616 for every employment type, which is what a default Headcount that "includes all current employees" would show if contractors and interns are loaded as employees. Both take the period end: Visier's validUntil instant (for January, January 31 at 23:59:59.999) and the warehouse's period-end snapshot_date, on which a leaver still counts. Never sum it over days. Decision (as in reconciliation.md and section 4.1 of the migration plan): keep both. A population flag on dim_employee reproduces the tenant's Headcount population (isActiveEmployee plus any filter added to the Headcount formula) and 'Headcount' follows it; the current measure is labelled 'Headcount (full-time employees)', not 'FTE headcount', because FTE is a separate factor in Visier. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Tutorials/data-model-query/aggregate-query-perform.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Platform/use-cases/build.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-time.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Release%20Notes/2019/SP19-release-notes.htm

definition: on Employee forInstantsInInterval(interval, month) filterBy(isActiveEmployee) aggregate averageOverTime(count(EmployeeID)): the trapezoid rule over month-end headcounts, so a single month is (opening + closing month end) / 2.
bigquery_target: analytics.fct_headcount_daily (FTE rows / days in the period); analytics.rpt_workforce_daily (sum(headcount) / count_distinct(snapshot_date))
notes: Different method: the warehouse takes the mean of every day's FTE headcount, Visier averages month-end instants. Q3 2026: daily mean 584.4; from the month ends (574 on 2026-06-30, 582, 589, 595 on 2026-09-30) the trapezoid gives (574/2 + 582 + 589 + 595/2) / 3 = 585.2. Visier's example only shows one month, so the weights for a quarter are our inference, to confirm against a tenant export (open question 4). With every employment type the month-end (trapezoid) average is 617.00 for Q3 2026 and 515.33 for 2025; contractors and interns add 31.83 and 20.96 after the method step (reconciliation.md). Decision: keep the daily mean as the warehouse definition (it is the attrition denominator) and add a Visier-compatible month-end measure, built on dim_date.is_month_end, for the parallel run. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm

definition: Numerator of Turnover Rate ("Turnover Count divided by Average Headcount"). Visier's other pages name the exit count Employee Exit Count, a metric that is additive over time. Whether the tenant's Turnover Count is a plain count of Employee_Exit events is read from its metric Settings.
notes: Q3 2026: 24 FTE exits. Contract and internship ends (END_OF_TERM) are left out of fct_terminations; with every employment type there are 41 exits in Q3 2026 (24 + 17) and 107 in 2025 (77 + 30). See reconciliation.md. Counts exit events: a rehired person has two employee_ids here and can leave twice. If the tenant loaded rehires under their original EmployeeID instead, compare by person_id. Expected variance classes against a tenant: exits Visier generates (System Termination) or infers from temporal loads, which have no source record, and the next-period rule (see Employee_Exit). Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/solution%20settings/aggregate-thresholds-set.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-create.htm

definition: "Turnover Rate is calculated as the Turnover Count divided by Average Headcount". Visier can produce annualised and trailing-12-month versions as separate metrics: Annualized and Annualized Rate are derived metric types, and its formula language has annualize() (annualize(EmployeeExitRate)) and trailing12Months() (trailing12Months(EmployeeExitCount)).
bigquery_target: analytics.fct_headcount_daily joined to analytics.fct_terminations (leavers / avg_headcount); analytics.rpt_workforce_daily (sum(exits) / average headcount)
grain: One value per period; not additive
notes: Same structure; the warehouse calls it attrition rate. Q3 2026: 24 / 584.4 = 4.11%; with the full-time month-end average (585.2) it would be 4.10%. The largest difference is the population: counting contractors and interns adds 17 exits (7 contract and 10 internship ends) and lifts the month-end average to 617.00, so Q3 2026 reads 6.65% (41 / 617.00) against 4.11%, and 2025 20.76% (107 / 515.33) against 15.57% (reconciliation.md). It can also differ through exit-period attribution, system terminations and annualisation: the warehouse rate is for the period and not annualised, while Visier's annualize() works on the Gregorian calendar. Visier's benchmark comparison metric for all exits is Employee Exit Rate; check in the Data Model API metric list whether the tenant's Turnover Rate and Employee Exit Rate are the same metric. The tenant's denominators are read from each metric's Settings tab during the inventory, not assumed. Decision: keep 'Turnover Rate (full-time employees)' as the current definition and add 'Turnover Rate (all employees)' if the tenant counts contingent workers, which needs contractor and intern exits in a mart (today they stop at staging). Ship period rates now; add annualised and trailing-12-month rates only if the tenant's dashboards use them. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/solution%20settings/aggregate-thresholds-set.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/metrics/visier-formula-language.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-create.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Visier%20People%20Metrics/benchmarks/benchmarks%20visier.htm

definition: Rate of resignations: in Visier's Employee Exit Model, Resignation Count is one child of Voluntary Turnover Count, and "Resignations do not include retirements". The denominator is read from the tenant's metric Settings (Visier documents Average Headcount for Turnover Rate).
notes: Naming trap: the warehouse's 'voluntary' is Visier's Resignation, not Voluntary Turnover. Q3 2026: 20 resignations, 20 / 584.4 = 3.42%. This assumes the tenant files every VOL_* reason under Resignation and none under Other Voluntary Turnover, which is an open question. Decision: label the LookML measures Resignation Count and Resignation Rate (Visier's benchmark name) at cut-over, keeping the field names so saved content still works. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/concepts.htm https://www.visier.com/research/resignation-report/ https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Visier%20People%20Metrics/benchmarks/benchmarks%20visier.htm

visier_item: Voluntary Turnover Rate (and Voluntary Turnover Count)
definition: Rate of voluntary exits, where "Resignation Count, Retirement Count, and Other Voluntary Turnover Count ... sum up to the Voluntary Turnover Count". The denominator is read from the tenant's metric Settings.
bigquery_target: analytics.rpt_workforce_daily (voluntary_exits + retirement_exits); analytics.fct_terminations where termination_type in ('voluntary', 'retirement')
notes: Visier's Voluntary Turnover includes retirement; the warehouse's voluntary does not. Q3 2026: 20 voluntary + 1 retirement = 21 exits, 21 / 584.4 = 3.59% on the warehouse's full-time daily-mean denominator (3.40%, 21 / 617.00, on the month-end average with every employment type; see reconciliation.md), against 3.42% for the warehouse's voluntary rate. The data is there (rpt_workforce_daily has both columns) but no LookML measure includes retirement. Decision: add voluntary turnover measures (voluntary or retirement) under Visier's name, so the tenant's figure is never compared with the warehouse's voluntary rate. P2: the risk at cut-over is the naming trap, which reconciliation.md checks on every run. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/concepts.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Visier%20People%20Metrics/benchmarks/benchmarks%20visier.htm

definition: on Employee_Exit filterBy(isExitActualRetirement) aggregate count(EmployeeID): exits that were retirements.
notes: Direct match: one type code (R) and one reason (RET_RETIREMENT). Q3 2026: 1. No dedicated LookML measure: filter Exit Type = retirement on Leavers. Retirement Rate is a Visier benchmark name; not built. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Visier%20People%20Metrics/benchmarks/benchmarks%20visier.htm

definition: Rate of exits the organization initiated (denominator from the tenant's metric Settings); Visier's exit attributes for these include Termination, Other Involuntary and Reduction in Force, and its Termination Count filters on isExitActualTermination.
notes: Q3 2026: 3 / 584.4 = 0.51%. Which reasons the tenant's concepts count as Termination, Reduction in Force and Other Involuntary is not public. Proposed for confirmation: INV_PERFORMANCE and INV_MISCONDUCT to Termination, INV_RESTRUCTURING to Reduction in Force. END_OF_TERM only ends contractor and intern records, which fct_terminations leaves out. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/analytic-objects/events-create.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Visier%20People%20Metrics/benchmarks/benchmarks%20visier.htm

visier_item: Regretted Resignation Rate (tenant-defined, no Visier standard)
definition: No Visier standard: Visier docs use "regrettable employee exits" only as an example population. Tenant definition to confirm: voluntary exits the manager marked as regretted, divided by average headcount.
notes: A tenant extension, not Visier standard content. Q3 2026: 10 regretted exits, 10 / 584.4 = 1.71% (half of the 20 resignations). The flag is set only on voluntary exits (null for involuntary exits and retirements). Open questions: is it an exit attribute or derived from performance data (a Visier blog ties regrettable turnover to performance), and is it reported as a rate on headcount or as a share of exits? Decision: keep the HRIS exit flag and label the metric as tenant-defined. Not reconciled: there is no Visier definition to emulate until the client gives its own. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytics/analyses/analyses-ai-explore.htm https://www.visier.com/blog/ask-visier-why-are-your-employees-resigning/

definition: Exit attribute classifying the exit. A Visier blog breaks turnover down "by exit type: resignation, involuntary turnover, and retirement"; the tenant's members are read from the Data Model API. Visier's Employee Exit example lists Exit Type beside separate exit attributes (Resignation, Retirement, Termination, Other Voluntary, Other Involuntary, Reduction in Force, System Termination), and its metric examples treat retirement, resignation and termination as concepts (isExitActualRetirement, isExitActualResignation, isExitActualTermination).
notes: The three warehouse types line up with the blog's three exit types (voluntary to resignation, involuntary to involuntary turnover, retirement to retirement). Retirement is its own type in both, but Visier counts it inside Voluntary Turnover. The finer split is the Employee Exit Model, which Visier defines from the Employee Exit Reason dimension, so it maps by reason_code (see Employee Exit Model). The full mapping belongs in the termination_reasons seed (proposed exit-category column). Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/analytic-objects/events-create.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/concepts.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm https://www.visier.com/blog/ask-visier-why-are-your-employees-resigning/

definition: Exit attribute recording why the employee left; Visier lists Employee Exit Reason among the Employee_Exit event's example attributes.
notes: Codes come from the HRIS and plain-English names from the termination_reasons seed, which must gain a new code before the source uses it (data contract). The tenant's reason members are read from the Data Model API (dimension members) and compared with the seed. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/analytic-objects/events-create.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/apis/analytic-model/data-model/data-model-api.htm

definition: Calculation concept: a hierarchy in which child counts sum to a parent count, for example Resignation, Retirement and Other Voluntary Turnover Counts summing to Voluntary Turnover Count.
bigquery_target: termination_reasons seed (reason_code to termination_type_code, plus a proposed exit-category column) behind analytics.fct_terminations
notes: The warehouse has a flat type per reason, not Visier's hierarchy. Visier defines this hierarchy from the Employee Exit Reason dimension, so it maps by reason_code. Decision: add an exit-category column, and its voluntary or involuntary parent, to the termination_reasons seed, filled from the tenant's concept configuration, so Resignation, Voluntary Turnover and Termination counts come from one mapping. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/concepts.htm

definition: Events Visier generates "to fill in gaps" in incomplete data, because all start and termination events must be balanced.
original_source_system: HRIS: no source record (Visier generates them from gaps in hris_employees and hris_terminations)
grain: One generated event per unbalanced member
notes: Not rebuilt: the warehouse only has exits recorded in hris_terminations, and the source tests reject exits for unknown employees. Exits Visier generates, or infers when a member disappears from a temporal load, become a named variance class in the reconciliation instead of warehouse rows. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/analytic-objects/system-events.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/data/data-loads.htm

definition: Visier's Tenure metric is average(Tenure / 12) over active employees, in years and not additive, where Tenure is the calculated property monthsBetween(Start_Date, effectiveDate, gregorian).
grain: One value per day; use the last day of the period
notes: Both are evaluated at an instant: the warehouse at the snapshot date, never today. Units differ (months from monthsBetween against days / 365.25), so expect differences of a fraction of a month. 2026-09-30: mean 2.76 years. Rehires: the warehouse restarts tenure at the new hire_date; Visier depends on which date the tenant's Tenure uses (Start_Date or Hire Date; open question 7). One FTE employed on 2026-09-30 is a rehire, so the effect is small today. Tenure at exit (Q3 2026 leavers: 2.03 years) corresponds to Employee Exit Average Tenure ("The average tenure, in years, of employees who exited the organization during the period"), which appears in the example metric list of Visier's aggregate-query tutorial; its start date is as unconfirmed as Tenure's. The median has no Visier counterpart in the docs reviewed: confirm whether the tenant reports it. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Tutorials/data-model-query/aggregate-query-perform.htm

definition: Calculated property monthsBetween(Start_Date, effectiveDate, gregorian): tenure in months, re-evaluated at whatever instant is analysed.
grain: One value per employee per day (per exit for tenure at exit)
notes: Calculated properties become expressions evaluated as of a date: tenure on a day is a LookML dimension in the headcount explore (not stored), and tenure at exit is stored on fct_terminations. Years here, months in Visier. Visier describes it two ways: the metric-examples tutorial computes it from Start_Date, and the objects page says Tenure "takes the simple property Hire Date" ("time from Latest Time to Hire Date"). Which date the tenant uses, and for rehires, is open question 7. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/properties/properties.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/getting%20started/objects-visier-cloud.htm

definition: Visier has a Tenure Range dimension that groups employees by tenure; its band edges are not public.
grain: One value per employee per day (per exit for tenure at exit)
notes: Warehouse bands: under 1, 1-3, 3-5 and 5+ years. Labels already differ between LookML ('Under 1 year') and the reporting views ('< 1 year'). Decision: copy the tenant's band edges into one seed and use it in both LookML and the reporting views, replacing the two hard-coded case expressions. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytics/visual%20types/drivers.htm

definition: A parent-child dimension shared between Employee and Managed Position (it can also be shared with Requisition), with levels named Level 1, Level 2 and so on.
grain: One row per department or team
notes: Two levels here: division_name is Level 1 and department_name the team (Engineering has three teams under a parent that holds only its head). Membership is as-was, through each version's department_id; names and parents are as they are today, because dim_org keeps no history. Visier docs say customers most commonly provide as-was hierarchies; which one the tenant uses is an open question. The same dim_org serves requisitions and applications through department_id, and division_name is the row-level security key in every explore. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/swp/Organization%20Design/data-requirements.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/dimensions/dimensions.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/dimensions/parent-child/parent-child-configure.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/data/data-loads.htm

definition: Tenant-specific property to confirm (name and any location hierarchy): the work location of the employee's job version.
bigquery_target: analytics.dim_employee.location (copied to fct_headcount_daily, fct_hires and fct_terminations)
notes: Five flat values (Bengaluru, London, New York, Remote, Singapore), no country or region level. In Visier data is mapped to properties and dimensions are built on them, so a leveled location dimension in the tenant would need a mapping seed here. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/dimensions/dimensions.htm

definition: Tenant-specific property to confirm (name and ordering): the grade of the job version, L1 (entry) to L7.
grain: One value per job version (per requisition for requisitions)
lookml_field: dim_employee.job_level; dim_employee.job_level_number; fct_headcount_daily.job_level; fct_hires.job_level; fct_terminations.job_level; fct_requisitions.job_level
notes: job_level_number gives the order for range filters. On a requisition it is the hire's starting level once filled, otherwise the seat's current grade. The source contract warns if the 'L1' form changes. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/apis/analytic-model/data-model/data-model-api.htm

definition: A forward reference from an employee to their manager (many-to-one, which Visier's glossary likens to a foreign key and inner join).
notes: manager_id is an employee_id, so it points at the manager's employment record (a rehired manager gets a new id). Reaching the manager's own attributes is a self-join on dim_employee that the explores don't offer today. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/swp/Organization%20Design/data-requirements.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Platform/key-terms.htm

definition: Parent-child dimension of managers built from the Direct_Manager reference; Visier's dynamic security filters follow a user's position in a hierarchy automatically.
bigquery_target: None yet: proposed manager-to-employee closure table built nightly from analytics.dim_employee.manager_id
grain: One row per manager and employee below them, per day (proposed)
notes: Not built: the warehouse scopes rows by division only. Needed if the tenant's permissions use dynamic filters on the manager hierarchy, or if managers analyse their whole team (open question). The closure table would also back a Looker access filter for managers. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/dimensions/dimensions.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/permissions/data%20security/security%20filters.htm

definition: "The set of positions that the organization is managing"; it shares the Organization_Hierarchy dimension with Employee.
bigquery_target: No mart (staged as stg_hris__positions); position_id on analytics.dim_employee, analytics.fct_requisitions and analytics.fct_hires
grain: One row per seat (in the source)
notes: Use Visier's name, not 'Position'. Seats, vacancies and is_filled are not modelled beyond fct_requisitions.is_backfill. The object type is inferred from the shared hierarchy, so confirm it in the tenant's Data Model API listing. Decision: build a position mart only if the tenant uses Managed Position analyses (vacancies, organization design). Sources: https://www.visier.com/docs/definitions/successfactors https://docs.visier.com/swp/Organization%20Design/data-requirements.htm

definition: "An employee was placed in a different position within the organization"; a promotion is Internal_Placement filtered by the isPromotion concept.
bigquery_target: None yet: job changes are versions of analytics.dim_employee with change_reason
notes: No movement fact yet. Proposed fct_internal_placements from consecutive dim_employee versions (the warehouse counterpart of VFL changes and previousChanges) with an is_promotion flag. It would give Promotion Rate (a Visier benchmark name; a 2019 Visier release described Employees with Promotions Rate as a percentage of end-of-period headcount) and transfers in and out for the headcount walk. Sources: https://www.visier.com/docs/definitions/successfactors https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/metrics/visier-formula-language.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Release%20Notes/2019/SU19-release-notes.htm

definition: Not an analytic object: Visier analyses time through each object's granularity and a business calendar; "The Gregorian calendar is Visier's default calendar", and an uploaded calendar sets period labels such as "FY 2020".
original_source_system: Warehouse: generated in dbt (no HRIS or ATS table)
grain: One row per calendar day, 2023-01-01 to 2027-12-31
lookml_field: dim_date.day_date; dim_date.year_quarter; dim_date.fiscal_year; dim_date.fiscal_quarter; dim_date.is_month_end; dim_date.is_quarter_end
notes: Listed so period definitions are checked. The fiscal year runs April to March and is named after the year it ends (FY2027 = 2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31). Open questions: is a business calendar the tenant's default, and do key metrics still use gregorian in their formulas? Visier only offers periods at or above an object's granularity, so the parallel run compares month ends. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Studio/data/business-calendar-upload.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Studio/data/business-calendar-requirements.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-time.htm

definition: "A request for one or more new employees", whose status and status effective date are captured.
notes: Each ATS requisition is for one seat. Requisitions counts by opened date and Open Requisitions is as of the reporting date; an equivalent of Visier's 'Requisitions Active in Period' is not built. Visier's docs name Requisition a subject: its glossary gives requisitions as an example of a subject, the Organization dimension "is shared by the subjects Employee and Requisition", and "Open Requisition Count calculates data from the Requisition subject". Sources: https://www.visier.com/docs/definitions/successfactors https://www.visier.com/docs/descriptions/application/vp-talent-acquisition/ https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Release%20Notes/2019/SU19-release-notes.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Platform/key-terms.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/dimensions/dimensions.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm

definition: Process concept: stages and outcomes defined on a status dimension; which requisition status the tenant uses is to confirm.
notes: The ATS has three statuses: Open, then Filled (offer accepted) or Cancelled. opened_date and closed_date give the status on any past date; any intermediate statuses the tenant tracks (for example an approval step) have no source equivalent. Map the tenant's stage and outcome names when the concept is read. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/process/process-configure.htm https://www.visier.com/docs/descriptions/application/vp-talent-acquisition/

definition: Tenant-specific property to confirm (name, and whether it is a reference to Employee): the employee who owns the requisition.
notes: An employee_id, so it can join to dim_employee for the manager's department or level (not joined in the recruiting explore today). Visier security files can map users to RequisitionID or ApplicantID; whether the tenant scopes recruiting data by hiring manager is an open question. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/permissions/security-from-file.htm

definition: Visier's glossary: days "from the date a job requisition is approved to the date an offer is accepted"; the product derives it from requisition status changes and their effective dates.
notes: Start point differs on paper: the warehouse starts at opened_date and the ATS has no separate approval date (requisitions are opened once approved), so the two are treated as the same day, to confirm. Another Visier glossary starts the clock "after advertising a position". Q3 2026, 40 FTE requisitions filled: mean 52.6 days, median 47; whether the tenant reports a mean or a median is not public. Decision: keep the start status configurable if the tenant's differs. Sources: https://visier.com/blog/hr-glossary-time-to-fill https://www.visier.com/blog/the-hr-terms-glossary/ https://www.visier.com/docs/descriptions/application/vp-talent-acquisition/

definition: "A candidate's application for a particular requisition": an application, not a person (the person is a Candidate).
notes: Same grain as Visier. Double submissions are removed (the first per candidate and requisition is kept). Visier tracks an applicant's stage over time; the warehouse keeps one row with the time each stage was reached, so the stage on a past date is not modelled. Applications counts by applied date; Visier's 'Applicants Active in Period' is not built. Sources: https://www.visier.com/docs/definitions/successfactors https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/getting%20started/objects-visier-cloud.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Release%20Notes/2019/SU19-release-notes.htm

definition: The status dimension Visier's Applicant Process is defined on, with stages Pre-Applied, Applied, Screened, Qualified, Interviews Started, Interviews Completed, Selected, Offered, Offer Accepted and Background Checked.
notes: Four in-progress stages here (applied, screen, interview, offer) against Visier's ten. Proposed mapping, to confirm against the tenant's list: applied to Applied, screen to Screened, interview to Interviews Started, offer to Offered, hired to Offer Accepted. Pre-Applied, Qualified, Interviews Completed, Selected and Background Checked have no source stage. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/process/process-configure.htm

definition: Process concept over Applicant Stage with the success outcome "Hired Yet to Start" and the failure outcomes Abandoned, Rejected and System Rejected.
notes: Outcomes line up: the warehouse's hired means the offer was accepted, not that the person has started, which is Visier's "Hired Yet to Start". rejected maps to Rejected; withdrawn and offer_declined to Abandoned, to confirm. There is no System Rejected equivalent. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/process/process-configure.htm

definition: In Spring 2021 Visier changed the listed "Count in <X> Stage" metrics (Interview, Campus, Requisition, Recruiter and Business, and Learning Activity processes) to count only those currently at the stage; they used to count at or past it. The Applicant Process is not in that list, so confirm its stage metrics in the tenant. Summer 2026 added an Active in Stage (Applicant Process) metric: applicants "currently active or were active in the selected stage during the period". AtOrPastStage filters give the at-or-past count.
grain: One value per cohort of applications (applied date)
notes: The warehouse counts are at-or-past (reached the stage), which matches AtOrPastStage, not a currently-at-stage count or Active in Stage. FTE applications submitted in 2025: 2,833 screened, 931 interviewed, 209 offered. Decision: keep the 'reached' meaning and add currently-in-stage counts only if the tenant's dashboards use them. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Release%20Notes/2021/SP21-release-notes.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Release%20Notes/2026/SU26-release-notes.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/process/process-configure.htm

definition: Tenant-specific definition to confirm: for a cohort of applications, the share reaching each stage out of those that reached the stage before, and applications to accepted offers overall.
grain: One value per cohort of applications (applied date)
notes: Built from the at-or-past stage counts, on a cohort old enough to have finished. FTE applications submitted in 2025: 25.2% screened, 32.9% of those interviewed, 22.4% of those offered; 1.4% of applications ended in an accepted offer. No standard Visier conversion formula was found in the docs reviewed for this inventory: take the tenant's from its metric Settings if one exists. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/process/process-configure.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-create.htm

definition: Tenant-specific property to confirm (name and members): where the candidate came from.
notes: Five values: Agency, Careers Site, Job Board, LinkedIn, Referral. It is stored on the application, so a candidate who applies twice can have two sources. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/apis/analytic-model/data-model/data-model-api.htm

definition: "An event that records the hire of an applicant", separate from the Employment Start event on the HR side.
grain: One row per application with an accepted offer
notes: The recruiting tables count a hire when the offer is accepted (Q3 2026: 40 FTE offers accepted); fct_hires counts the first day at work (Q3 2026: 45 FTE starts). Both are kept and every figure says which one it uses. Source: https://www.visier.com/docs/definitions/workday

definition: "An event that records the close of an offer", where an Offer is "an offer of employment made to an applicant".
grain: One row per application with an answered offer
notes: The source allows one offer per application, so offers live on the application row rather than in their own table. offer_answered is the accepted or declined time. Source: https://www.visier.com/docs/definitions/successfactors

definition: No Visier standard metric: Visier has Offer and Offer Close objects and Offered and Offer Accepted stages but no public formula. Tenant definition to confirm: offers accepted / offers answered (accepted or declined) in the period.
grain: One value per period (offer answered date)
notes: Q3 2026: 40 / (40 + 10) = 80.0%. A common alternative divides by every offer extended, including those still waiting; ask which denominator the client uses. Sources: https://www.visier.com/docs/definitions/successfactors https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/concepts/process/process-configure.htm

definition: Days from the moment the candidate applies "until they accept the offer"; Visier holds Time to Hire as a property of the Employee Start event.
bigquery_target: analytics.rpt_recruiting_funnel.days_to_hire and a LookML dimension on fct_application_funnel (applied_date to hired_at, by offer accepted date); analytics.fct_hires.days_to_hire (by start date)
notes: Same span. Because Visier attaches it to Employee Start, compare against fct_hires grouped by hire_date (Q3 2026 starts: mean 25.5 days, median 25), not the funnel measures grouped by offer accepted date (Q3 2026 offers: mean 26.2 days, median 25). Another Visier post starts the clock at "applying or being sourced"; the source has no sourcing date. Sources: https://www.visier.com/hr-metrics/ https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/getting%20started/objects-visier-cloud.htm https://www.visier.com/blog/top-strategic-hr-metrics/

definition: A property of the Employee Start event ("Hire Date, Hire Type, and Time to Hire are properties of the Employee Start event"); its members are tenant-specific.
notes: Two members here (new hire, rehire), from the first job version's change_reason. A rehire is a new employee_id with the same person_id (matched on email). Confirm the tenant's members. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/getting%20started/objects-visier-cloud.htm

definition: Benchmark values Visier provides for a set of metrics, including Resignation Rate, Retirement Rate, Voluntary Turnover Rate, Involuntary Turnover Rate, Employee Exit Rate, Employee Starts Rate, Promotion Rate, Manager Ratio and Headcount Percent of Total.
original_source_system: None: provided by Visier, not by the HRIS or ATS
bigquery_target: Not rebuilt; the comparable tenant rates are in analytics.fct_headcount_daily and analytics.fct_terminations
grain: One value per benchmark metric and group
notes: No warehouse equivalent: the values come from Visier, not from the tenant's data. Open question: does the client use Benchmarks, and does anyone need a replacement? The warehouse reuses the benchmark metric names as labels so its rates stay recognisable. Visier's objects page calls benchmarks an overlay; the row is typed metric because the inventory has no overlay type. The other out-of-scope items (predictions, plans, internal comparisons, other overlays, Vee and the Visier MCP server) are retired in section 1 of the migration plan, not listed as rows. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Visier%20People%20Metrics/benchmarks/benchmarks%20visier.htm https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/getting%20started/objects-visier-cloud.htm

definition: Tenant-specific property to confirm (name, and whether the tenant holds pay as a multi-value property): annual base salary and its currency on each job version.
notes: The most sensitive property. Visier data access sets grant Detailed, Aggregate or None per property, and Visier warns that users "can still infer sensitive values, such as compensation, from aggregate values" and recommends None. Here both fields are hidden LookML dimensions behind the can_see_salary access grant; Aggregate access has no one-to-one Looker equivalent (section 6 of the migration plan). Never sum or average across currencies. first_name, last_name and email are not gated in LookML today; the plan proposes a PII policy tag for them. Open question: which permissions give compensation Detailed or Aggregate access. Source: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Studio/permissions/data%20security/data%20access%20sets.htm

definition: Promotion Events Count is on priorState(Internal_Placement) filterBy(isPromotion) aggregate count(EmployeeID), grouped by the job the person was promoted from; Promotion Rate is a Visier benchmark name. In 2019 Visier described Employees with Promotions Rate as "a percentage of end of period headcount"; the tenant's denominator is read from its metric Settings.
bigquery_target: None yet: proposed fct_internal_placements (is_promotion) from consecutive analytics.dim_employee versions
notes: No promotion measure yet. The data is there: dim_employee holds 346 job versions with change_reason promotion (and 50 with transfer) over the whole history. Built on the proposed fct_internal_placements (see Internal_Placement), with the previous version's attributes for Visier's priorState grouping. Sources: https://docs.visier.com/developer/Analytic%20Model/metrics/metrics-examples.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Visier%20People%20Metrics/benchmarks/benchmarks%20visier.htm https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Release%20Notes/2019/SU19-release-notes.htm

visier_item: 90 Day / 1 Year Resignation Rate of New Starts
definition: Added in Spring 2026 as benchmarks and as comparison metrics on the tenant's own data: "the percentage of starts that end in a resignation within a 90 day or 1 year time period", tracking groups of new hires by start date. They replace the New Hire 90 Day Resignation Rate and New Hire Resignation Rate benchmarks.
bigquery_target: None yet: start cohorts from analytics.fct_hires joined to analytics.fct_terminations on employee_id
notes: Not built: no measure follows a start cohort to its exits. Both facts carry employee_id, so a cohort model is a join; a 1 year rate is final only for cohorts that started more than a year before the reporting date, and fct_hires starts on 2023-10-01. Whether the tenant reports these is part of the Benchmarks question. Source: https://docs.visier.com/visier-people/Release%20Notes/2026/SP26-release-notes.htm
